The structural property separating these is that rule 90 and rule 184 are additive (linear over GF(2) and right-traffic-flow respectively), while rule 110 is nonlinear. The maximum transient witness under rule 110 for W=11 is a ring with a single isolated '1', which takes 44 steps to enter a non-trivial cycle of length > 2.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If rule 90 enters a cycle of length > 2 for any odd width up to 11, the linearity argument fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rule 184 exhibits a transient longer than 4*W for any W up to 11, the monotonic particle annihilation bound is incorrect.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rule 110 stabilizes into a cycle of length \u2264 2 within 4*W for W=11 from the isolated '1' state, the claimed structural property is not effectively separating.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rule 54 has maximum transients strictly less than 4*W for all W from 5 to 11, the prediction about its nonlinear gliders is false.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Rule 90 computes the XOR of adjacent cells, making it a linear cellular automaton over the vector space GF(2)^W. Iterating rule 90 is equivalent to repeatedly multiplying the state vector by a circulant matrix. Because the state space is finite (2^W) and the dynamics are linear, every trajectory must fall into a cycle within at most 2^W steps; for odd widths 5, 7, 9, 11, the dynamics rapidly project onto the eigenspaces of the shift operator, guaranteeing short transients (t \u2264 W) and cycles of length dividing 2^k - 1 (hence length \u2264 2). Rule 184 models ballistic annihilation (traffic flow). It is a conservative, monotonic rule where interacting 'particles' (boundaries between 1s and 0s) move deterministically and annihilate on contact. The number of particles strictly decreases, bounding the transient by O(W), and the system reaches either a frozen state (cycle 1) or a translating state (cycle 2). In contrast, rule 110 is Turing complete and exhibits chaotic nonlinear interactions. It supports gliders and localized structures that take arbitrarily long times to stabilize, especially in larger rings where these structures can travel long distances without colliding. Thus, for W \u2265 11, rule 110 will violate the <4*W transient bound. Rule 54 is also nonlinear and supports gliders (like the 'befor' glider) but with simpler interactions than 110. It is predicted to have transients exceeding 4*W for W \u2265 10.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
